physicalNotes: Radius: Radius 0.141 ± 0.007 solar radii measured with VLTI/AMBER by Demory et al. (2009), A&A 505, 205. Kervella, Thévenin and Lovis (2017) give 0.1542 ± 0.0045 from a radius to magnitude relation; the interferometric value is adopted. Adopted 98,094 km, 0.1410 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.1221 ± 0.0022 solar masses from Kervella, Thévenin & Lovis (2017), A&A 598, L7 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.03495), the value they adopt for Proxima: gravitational parameter 16,204,188,929 km^3/s^2 at 132,712,440,041.94 km^3/s^2 per solar mass. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is adopted.

sources.position: SIMBAD basic record for NAME Proxima Centauri (HIP 70890), ICRS J2000 position, reference 2020yCat.1350....0G, retrieved 2026-09-21: https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=Proxima+Centauri
sources.distance: Inverse of the Gaia EDR3 parallax 768.0665 ± 0.0499 mas via SIMBAD
sources.binary: Kervella, Thévenin & Lovis (2017), A&A 598, L7 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.03495) measure Proxima's radial velocity against Alpha Centauri's and find Proxima and Alpha Centauri gravitationally bound with a high degree of confidence. This record adopts no orbit of Proxima, so the star is placed by its own astrometry and carries no orbit.
